finding: Immutable deployment identity and generated-hostname response observation are distinct evidence layers. A successful direct HTTPS HEAD or GET response may establish only that the exact generated hostname returned a successful response at the observation time; it cannot establish content correctness, alias promotion, audio routing, browser execution, or physical-device behavior.

primary_standard.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
relevance: HEAD is a defined safe read method whose response is equivalent to GET apart from response content.
3xx status codes require additional action and therefore cannot prove a direct generated-hostname response without recording redirects.

uncertainty: No live generated hostname was requested in this run.
Deployment Protection may produce authentication responses; those are retained as observations but do not satisfy public reachability.
A 2xx response does not establish expected application content or media behavior.
falsification_routes: Provide a verified deployment evidence envelope and an observation whose requested or final URL differs from the generated hostname; the contract must reject it.
Provide a redirect, TLS failure, network error, non-2xx response, unsafe method, or malformed timestamp; the contract must reject it.
Run the same normalized observation with reordered object fields; the canonical digest must remain stable.
